items.title: Outcomes in Seronegative Rheumatoid Arthritis and Undifferentiated Arthritis.
items.abstract: Seronegative rheumatoid arthritis (SNRA) and undifferentiated arthritis (UA) are heterogeneous conditions that are often reclassified to more specific diagnoses. We report a retrospective chart review from the United States military health system (MHS) that examines clinical characteristics, reclassification rates, and potential predictors of reclassification in SNRA and UA. The study included MHS beneficiaries diagnosed with SNRA or UA. Inclusion criteria consisted of a negative rheumatoid factor (RF) and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (CCP) antibody at presentation, synovitis on a rheumatologist's exam, and treatment with a disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drug (DMARD). We then recorded clinical characteristics including distributions of joint involvement, erosions or extra-articular disease, and the number of clinic visits. We used binomial logistic regression to evaluate for any predictors of future diagnostic reclassification. One hundred thirty-three patients were included, with an index diagnosis of SNRA in 20 (15%) patients, and UA in 113 (85%) patients. Eighty-five (63.9%) patients were later reclassified to other diagnoses, including SNRA (52.1%), seropositive rheumatoid arthritis (9.4%), psoriatic arthritis (14.6%), spondyloarthritis (14.6%), and other (9.4%). The regression model was statistically significant (X2(7) = 15.747, P = .028) and explained 15% of the variance in diagnostic reclassification. Although most variables failed to reach significance, more clinic visits predicted greater odds of diagnostic reclassification (OR 1.07, CI 1.03-1.12). Our data indicate a potential association with the frequency of follow-up with the likelihood of future diagnostic reclassification in SNRA and UA, suggesting that diagnostic accuracy may be higher in patients with more frequent follow-up visits.

items.title: A Systematic Literature Review on the Economic Burden of Sjögren's Disease.
items.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by exocrine glandular dysfunction, chronic fatigue, and pain, with considerable morbidity, mortality, and significant quality-of-life burden. The economic impact of SjD thus far has been underappreciated and understudied, limiting understanding of its implications for patients. Therefore, we conducted a systematic literature review to identify, evaluate, and summarize the economic burden on patients with SjD. The systematic literature review was developed using the PRISMA reporting guidelines for systematic reviews and conducted using the MEDLINE and Embase databases (via OvidSP), covering the period from January 1, 2014, to July 14, 2025. Additional searches were performed in the bibliographies of relevant studies, Google Scholar, disease-specific websites, and conference proceedings. Data regarding healthcare resource utilization (HCRU), direct medical costs, as well as indirect and societal costs were extracted. A focus group discussion of patients living with SjD generated qualitative insights to identify themes across diagnosis, treatment, and burden of disease. A total of 49 unique studies reported outcomes related to economic burden of SjD; HCRU was reported in 27 studies, while 21 studies reported direct or indirect costs, and 16 focused on productivity loss. The studies were performed across the globe, but predominately in North America (n = 22) and Europe (n = 16). Direct healthcare costs for patients with SjD were noted to be 1.6-3.1 times higher than for patients without SjD owing to more frequent hospitalizations, outpatient visits, emergency department care, and dental visits compared with patients without SjD. In addition, total indirect costs were around 2 times higher for patients with SjD than those without SjD, a consequence of substantial productivity loss, including activity impairment (27%-61%), overall work impairment (26%-38%), absenteeism (2.4%-27%), and presenteeism (21%-35%). Patients with SjD from the focus group reported frequent emergency care for SjD-related symptoms, high out-of-pocket medical costs (which includes over-the-counter medication cost and specialized diets), significant work and daily productivity loss due to fatigue and cognitive symptoms, and ongoing financial strain requiring community or family support. This systematic review demonstrates that SjD results in measurable healthcare costs, loss of productivity, and a notable financial burden on both individuals and healthcare systems, highlighting an increased need for urgent care, hospital admissions, and extended stays. Indirect costs, primarily arising from lost productivity, further amplify the economic burden of SjD. In total, these costs highlight the economic and societal burden of SjD, reflected in both direct healthcare costs and indirect costs.

items.title: Comorbidity burden and its impact on physical functioning and activities of daily living in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Comorbidities are highly prevalent in Systemic lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and are associated with increased morbidity and mortality. We investigated the association between cumulative comorbidity burden, physical function, and activities of daily living (ADLs) in SLE patients. In this cross-sectional study, we assessed comorbidity burden using the Age-Adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (ACCI) and Rheumatic Disease Comorbidity Index (RDCI) in 240 consecutive patients with SLE. Grip strength and dexterity were assessed using the Jamar dynamometer and Purdue pegboard test, respectively. ADLs were evaluated with the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (DASH) questionnaire and the Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ). We also assessed domains of the Lupus Quality of Life (LupusQoL) Questionnaire related to physical function and ADLs, including "Physical Health", "Pain", "Planning" and "Fatigue". Associations were examined using multivariate linear regression models adjusted for potential demographic and clinical confounders. Median (IQR) ACCI and RDCI scores were 2 (1-3) and 0 (0-2), respectively. In multivariate analysis, higher ACCI scores were associated with impaired dexterity (p < 0.001), reduced grip strength (p < 0.05) across all models, and higher DASH scores and poorer scores in the "Physical Health" and "Pain" domains, after adjustment for pain intensity and fibromyalgia (p < 0.05). Higher RDCI scores were associated with impaired dexterity (p < 0.01), poorer scores in the "Physical Health" domain across all models, and higher DASH scores in three models (p < 0.05). Comorbidity burden is independently associated with poorer physical functioning and ADLs performance in people with SLE.

items.title: Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Primary Biliary Cholangitis Overlap Syndrome in a 25-year-old Female: A Rare Case Report.
items.abstract: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) is an uncommon hematologic manifestation of systemic autoimmune diseases, most frequently associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic autoimmune cholestatic liver disorder that rarely coexists with SLE. An overlap syndrome involving AIHA, SLE, and PBC is exceptionally rare and poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report the case of a 25-year-old female presenting with progressive jaundice, fatigue, and pallor. Laboratory evaluation revealed hemolytic anemia with elevated lactate dehydrogenase, reticulocytosis, and a positive direct Coombs test, consistent with AIHA. Autoimmune serology demonstrated high-titer antinuclear antibody, anti-double-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid positivity, and hypocomplementemia, supporting SLE. Persistent cholestatic liver enzyme elevation, AMA-M2 positivity, and supportive imaging findings indicated PBC. The patient improved following corticosteroids, immunosuppressive therapy, and ursodeoxycholic acid. This case emphasizes the importance of early recognition of multisystem autoimmune overlap syndromes to guide appropriate management and improve outcomes. Résumé Contexte: L’anémie hémolytique auto-immune (AHAI) est une manifestation hématologique rare des maladies auto-immunes systémiques, le plus souvent associée au lupus érythémateux systémique (LES). La cholangite biliaire primitive (CBP) est une maladie hépatique cholestatique auto-immune chronique qui coexiste rarement avec le LES. Le syndrome de chevauchement associant AHAI, LES et CBP est exceptionnellement rare et pose d’importants défis diagnostiques et thérapeutiques. Présentation du cas: Nous rapportons le cas d’une femme de 25 ans présentant un ictère progressif, une fatigue et une pâleur. Les examens biologiques ont révélé une anémie hémolytique avec élévation de la lactate déshydrogénase, réticulocytose et test de Coombs direct positif, compatible avec une AHAI. Le bilan sérologique auto-immun a montré un titre élevé d’anticorps antinucléaires, une positivité des anticorps anti-ADN double brin et une hypocomplémentémie, étayant le diagnostic de LES. La persistance d’une élévation des enzymes hépatiques à prédominance cholestatique, associée à la positivité des anticorps antimitochondries de type M2 (AMA-M2) et à des résultats d’imagerie compatibles, a permis de retenir le diagnostic de CBP. La patiente a présenté une amélioration clinique et biologique après un traitement associant des corticostéroïdes, un traitement immunosuppresseur et de l’acide ursodésoxycholique. Conclusion: Ce cas souligne l’importance d’une reconnaissance précoce des syndromes de chevauchement auto-immuns multisystémiques afin d’orienter rapidement la prise en charge thérapeutique appropriée et d’améliorer le pronostic des patients.

items.title: Research progress of biomarkers in Sjögren disease.
items.abstract: Sjögren disease is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by immune-mediated dysregulation that leads to exocrine gland destruction, impaired tissue repair, and frequent co-occurrence with other connective tissue diseases. Current internationally accepted diagnostic criteria rely predominantly on a combination of characteristic clinical manifestations, autoantibody profiles, and histopathological findings from minor salivary gland biopsy. In early-stage disease, when immune-driven glandular injury has not yet caused evident structural damage, or when histopathological alterations are delayed compared to clinical symptoms, the conventional "gold standard" method may produce false-negative outcomes, leading to diagnostic delays or overlooked diagnoses. In recent years, advances in multi-omics platforms, single-cell technologies, and artificial intelligence-driven data analysis have enabled the discovery of a growing number of promising biomarkers, including proteases, metabolites, microRNAs, and novel autoantibody epitopes detectable in serum, saliva, and tears. Several of these candidates have already undergone translational validation and are beginning to impact clinical decision-making. This review highlights recent advancements in biomarker research for Sjögren disease, evaluating their diagnostic utility, prognostic relevance, and therapeutic implications.

items.title: Current Status and Temporal Changes in Lupus Nephritis in Japan: Analysis of the Japan Renal Biopsy Registry.
items.abstract: This study evaluated temporal changes in the clinical and histological features of lupus nephritis at first renal biopsy in Japan. This retrospective observational study used Japan Renal Biopsy Registry data. Patients undergoing their first renal biopsy in 2018-2021 were compared with a historical cohort from 2007 to 2012. Clinical characteristics and histological classes based on the International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society classification were compared. The study included 331 patients in the historical cohort and 682 in the recent cohort. The recent cohort was older (median age, 42 vs. 37 years; p = 0.014), with a higher proportion aged 60 years or older (19.2% vs. 10.6%; p < 0.001). Histological class distribution differed significantly between cohorts. Class IV (±V) lesions were less frequent in the recent cohort (34.3% vs. 44.1%), whereas Class II and Class III (±V) lesions were numerically more frequent. The lower odds of Class IV (±V) lesions persisted after adjustment for age group (odds ratio, 0.676; 95% confidence interval, 0.516-0.886; p = 0.005). Amongst patients with Class III/IV lesions, pure Class III lesions were more frequent and pure Class IV lesions were less frequent in the recent cohort. The recent first-biopsy cohort was older and had a lower proportion of Class IV (±V) lesions than the historical cohort, even after age adjustment. These findings suggest temporal changes in LN in Japan, although the greater proportion of missing histological classification data in the historical cohort should be considered when interpreting the histological differences.

items.title: Clinical Features, Treatments, and Outcomes of an International Cohort of 96 Children with Takayasu Arteritis.
items.abstract: To characterize the clinical features, treatment, and outcomes of a large, international cohort of childhood-onset Takayasu arteritis (cTAK). Patients with a diagnosis of cTAK were identified in A Registry of Childhood Vasculitis and divided into subcohorts by era-of diagnosis: pre-biologic (PB; 1986-2006), early biologic (EB; 2007-2017), and recently diagnosed (RD; 2018-present). Longitudinal patient data were collected at time of diagnosis (TOD), postinduction (PI; 3-6 months after TOD), and 12 months after TOD (12m). Meaningful clinical improvement was defined as at least a 50% reduction in the Pediatric Vasculitis Activity Score. Damage was assessed by the Pediatric Vasculitis Damage Index. Among 96 patients (69% female, median age 12.8 years [interquartile range 9.8-15.3]) from nine countries, 86% showed clinical improvement at PI and 90% maintained improvement at 12m. Glucocorticoids (GC; n = 84, 88%) and methotrexate (n = 47, 49%) were the two most common medications prescribed at TOD, often together and in combination with another medication. GC use continued at 12m in 79%. Patients more recently diagnosed were more likely to receive treatment with tumor necrosis factor inhibitors (0% PB, 26% EB, and 35% RD; P = 0.007) and reach 70% improvement (59% PB, 81% EB, and 100% RD; P = 0.007) at PI. However, neither improvement nor damage at 12m differed among the subcohorts. Although treatment approaches for cTAK have evolved and most patients demonstrate sustained clinical improvement at 12m, these advances have not translated into substantial changes in outcomes, highlighting the need for optimized therapeutic strategies.

items.title: [Systemic lupus erythematosus: new treatment targets and agents].
items.abstract: Management of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) has moved towards a defined treat-to-target approach. In April 2025 the first German S3 guideline was published, complementing the 2023 EULAR recommendations and the 2025 EULAR update on kidney involvement. All emphasize hydroxychloroquine as a backbone, a prednisolone target of ≤5mg/day and early use of belimumab or anifrolumab without any specific preference. Two validated targets guide therapy: DORIS remission (clinical SLEDAI 0, PGA <0,5, prednisolone ≤5mg/day) and LLDAS (SLEDAI-2K ≤4 without vital organ activity, PGA ≤1, prednisolone ≤7,5mg/day). Anifrolumab has been approved for subcutaneous self-administration in the EU since December 2025. Obinutuzumab, a type II anti-CD20 antibody, met its primary endpoint in the phase III trials REGENCY and ALLEGORY. Dapirolizumab pegol enabled glucocorticoid tapering alongside BICLA response in a phase III trial. Cellular approaches are advancing: autologous CD19 CAR T cells led to long-lasting remission in the refractory SLE patients, while off-the-shelf allogeneic constructs and T-cell engagers such as teclistamab or blinatumumab are in early clinical development. Im April 2025 erschien unter Federführung der DGRh die erste deutsche S3-Leitlinie zum SLE. 2025 wurde zudem das EULAR-Update zum SLE mit Nierenbeteiligung publiziert. Beide nennen Hydroxychloroquin als Basistherapie der 1. Wahl, eine Zieldosis von Prednisolon ≤5mg/Tag und den frühen Einsatz von Belimumab oder Anifrolumab.Beide Zielzustände sind validiert und in den Leitlinien verankert. DORIS erfordert einen klinischen SLEDAI von 0, PGA <0,5 und Prednisolon ≤5mg/Tag; LLDAS einen SLEDAI-2K ≤4 ohne organbedrohende Krankheitsaktivität, PGA ≤1 und Prednisolon ≤7,5mg/Tag.Anifrolumab ist seit Dezember 2025 in der EU auch subkutan (120mg/Woche) zugelassen. Obinutuzumab, ein Typ-II-Anti-CD20-Antikörper, erreichte in den Phase-III-Studien REGENCY (Lupus nephritis) und ALLEGORY (aktiver SLE) den primären Endpunkt. Belimumab zeigt auch in der „real-life“-Anwendung 25 Jahre nach Erstzulassung keine neuen Sicherheitsrisiken.Dapirolizumab pegol erreichte in Phase III eine Steroidreduktion auf ≤7,5mg/Tag kombiniert mit BICLA-Ansprechen bei 44,8 vs. 25,5%. Nach einmaliger Gabe autologer CD19-CAR-T-Zellen erreichten in einer Fallserie alle 8 SLE-Patienten eine DORIS-Remission bei vollständigem Absetzen der Immunsuppression. Der bispezifische T-Zell-Engager Teclistamab führte bei 5 refraktären Patienten zur Depletion von B-Zellen und Plasmazellen.

items.title: Severe ARDS and secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis complicating a flare of adult-onset Still's disease: a case-based review.
items.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare systemic inflammatory disorder in which parenchymal lung disease is an increasingly recognised complication, and macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) - that is, haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) secondary to an autoinflammatory or autoimmune condition (MAS-HLH) is a well-established one. Both carry disproportionately high morbidity and mortality. Although AOSD-associated lung disease and MAS-HLH are increasingly recognised as co-occurring manifestations of the same hyperinflammatory process, their combination, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) as the most severe form of lung involvement, remain under-reported. We report a 42-year-old woman with a background of AOSD who developed severe ARDS in the context of a five-week interruption of conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) around incision and drainage of a perianal abscess with complicating fistulous disease and a flare during that period. She developed severe hypoxaemic respiratory failure requiring intubation on the day of admission and later prone positioning, subsequently complicated by development of MAS-HLH, evidenced by hyperferritinaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia, fever and bone marrow-confirmed haemophagocytosis. Her disease trajectory was further complicated by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) reactivation. Management required sequential multi-target immunomodulation with corticosteroids, anakinra, ruxolitinib, tocilizumab and rituximab. She was mechanically ventilated for 19 days in intensive care and discharged from ICU on day 34 and from hospital following clinical stabilisation on day 73. This case illustrates that AOSD-related pulmonary disease can present as fulminant ARDS rather than the more indolent infiltrative patterns typically described and may be associated with other manifestations of AOSD including MAS-HLH. Because of concomitant infection and viral reactivation, the illness could not be attributed to AOSD alone. The case also describes survival following early multidisciplinary, multi-target immunomodulation delivered alongside antimicrobial cover, although the overlapping use of several agents precludes any conclusion about their individual or combined efficacy.

items.title: Rituximab for the treatment of calcinosis in dermatomyositis: A case series and review of the literature.
items.abstract: Dystrophic calcinosis, a frequent complication of dermatomyositis (DM) and juvenile DM (JDM) is poorly responsive to treatment. We analysed the outcomes of calcinosis in patients with idiopathic inflammatory myositis (IIM) and calcinosis treated with rituximab. IIM patients with calcinosis who received at least one cycle of rituximab (750 mg/m² in adults and 575 mg/m² in children on day 1 and day 14) were included. Baseline data included MMT8, patient global assessment, physician global assessment, myositis-specific and myositis-associated antibodies, duration, location and morphological pattern on plain radiographs of calcinosis. Improvement was defined as any reduction of calcinosis on plain radiographs. Of 224 IIM patients, 18 had calcinosis of whom 10 received rituximab (six JDM and four adult patients). Five of 10 patients were anti-NXP2, other MSAs were anti-MDA5, anti-PL7, and anti-Mi2. Seven of 10 patients had calcinosis at presentation; three developed subsequently. Predominant morphologies (radiographically) were nodular and sheet-like; two had mixed patterns. Eight of 10 patients also had active myositis (MITAX A or B) at rituximab initiation-of these, all showed either improvement or stabilization. Of the two with inactive disease treated solely for calcinosis, one stabilised; the other worsened. The one patient who worsened had diffuse distribution and mixed morphology of calcinosis. In this small series, rituximab initiation during active myositis was associated with improvement or stabilization of calcinosis; however, given the limited sample size, this observation should be interpreted cautiously and requires prospective validation.

items.title: Thrombophilia and Thrombosis in Behçet's Disease.
items.abstract: Behçet's disease is a systemic vasculitis that can affect all types of blood vessels in the body. The aim of our study was to determine the prevalence of hereditary thrombophilic factors that increase the risk of thrombosis in patients with Behçet's disease by comparing them with a healthy control group. This is a prospective cross-sectional study. We obtained peripheral blood samples from patients with Behçet's disease who visited our dermatology clinic within the last 15 months. We then genetically analyzed these samples using a thrombophilia kit in our medical genetics laboratory and statistically compared them with a healthy control group. A total of 197 participants were included in the study, comprising 98 Behçet's disease patients and 99 healthy controls. While the rate of the MTHFR (C677T) homozygous gene mutation was higher in the Behçet disease group (8.2%, n = 8) than in the healthy control group (5.1%, n = 5), no statistical difference was found between the two groups. No statistical difference was found between the two groups in terms of factor 13 mutation levels. The factor 2 mutation rate was higher in the Behçet group (5.1%, n = 5) than in the healthy control group, but no statistically significant difference was found between the two groups. The factor V Leiden mutation was detected as heterozygous in 9.2% of patients with Behçet's disease. Certain gene mutations were found at higher rates in our Behçet's patients than in the general population. It may be important to evaluate hereditary thrombophilic factors in Turkish Behçet's patients for managing complications.

items.title: Risk Factors and Risk Stratification of Acute Gout Flares after Orthopedic Surgery.
items.abstract: Considering the need for early recognition and appropriate perioperative management of gout to facilitate clinical decision making and improve surgical outcomes and patient prognosis, this study aimed to identify risk factors and establish a predictive model for acute gouty arthritis flares after orthopedic surgery. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 116 patients who underwent orthopedic surgery during 2021- 2025. The patients were categorized into flare (n = 55) and nonflare (n = 61) groups based on 1-year postoperative outcomes. Multivariate analysis revealed elevated serum uric acid (odds ratio [OR] = 1.029, P < .05), and greater blood loss (OR = 1.089, P < .05) as independent risk factors, while diabetes mellitus (OR = 0.014, P < .05) and intraoperative fluid infusion volume emerged as independent protective factors. Admission UA showed good predictive value (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.874), whereas the combined model showed high apparent discrimination, with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.970. Multiple perioperative factors can help predict postoperative gout flares. Using a combined model yielded high accuracy and could guide early risk stratification and personalized perioperative management. Nonetheless, prospective multicenter studies incorporating mechanistic biomarkers, longer follow-up, and external validation are needed to refine individualized perioperative gout management strategies.

items.title: Sarcopenia in Patients with Axial Spondyloarthritis: Associations with TNF Inhibitor Therapy and Exploratory Ultrasound Findings.
items.abstract: Sarcopenia has gained increasing attention as a potential comorbidity in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). This study aimed to assess the frequency of sarcopenia in patients with axSpA and to investigate its association with tumor necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) therapy. A secondary objective was to explore the potential value of ultrasound-based muscle measurements in identifying sarcopenia. This cross-sectional study enrolled 62 adult patients with axSpA who were evaluated during routine rheumatology follow-up. Clinical data, including disease activity, functional status, and spinal mobility, were recorded. Muscle strength, physical performance, and body composition were assessed in accordance with current sarcopenia definitions. Selected thigh and lumbar muscle parameters were measured using musculoskeletal ultrasound. Statistical analyses included comparative tests and regression modeling. Probable sarcopenia was identified in 22.6% of patients, while 12.9% met the criteria for sarcopenia; no cases of severe sarcopenia were detected. Sarcopenia was observed less frequently among patients receiving TNFi therapy compared with those not treated with TNFi. TNFi use was associated with a reduced likelihood of sarcopenia. Ultrasound measurements of the rectus femoris muscle showed modest associations with sarcopenia status, although their diagnostic performance was limited. Sarcopenia is common in patients with axSpA. In this cross-sectional study, TNFi use was associated with a lower prevalence of sarcopenia, although a causal relationship cannot be established. Ultrasound-derived muscle parameters showed limited discriminatory performance and should be considered exploratory.

items.title: Diaphragm Weakness and Sleep-Related Breathing Disorders in Patients with Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy.
items.abstract: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs) can cause respiratory muscle weakness, leading to diaphragm weakness (DW) and sleep-related breathing disorders (SRBD). We aimed to investigate clinical findings of DW and SRBD in patients with IIMs. In patients with biopsy-confirmed IIMs, demographics, respiratory symptoms, single-breath counting (SBC), arterial blood gas, upright/supine SpO2 and spirometry, diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO), maximal inspiratory and expiratory pressure (MIP, MEP), peak cough flow (PCF), and polysomnography parameters were prospectively evaluated. Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), STOP-BANG, and Mallampati scores were recorded. The presence of at least one of two findings was considered suggestive of DW: (1) paradoxical abdominal movement (PAM), (2) upright-supine forced vital capacity (FVC) difference of ≥20%. Sixteen patients (12 female/4 male, mean age: 54.4 ± 11.2/y, 9 dermatomyositis [DM], 6 polymyositis [PM], 1 inclusion body myositis [IBM]) were evaluated. Findings consistent with DW were observed in 25% of patients, and all of them had DM. MIP, MEP, and PCF were reduced in the majority of patients. Supine FVC% and supine SpO2 were significantly lower in patients with DW (P = .001 and P = .003, respectively). PaO2, SaO2, SBC, and PCF were lower, and the upright-supine SpO₂ difference was greater in patients with DW, although these differences were not statistically significant. Polysomnography was performed in 68.8% (n = 11) of patients. All 11 patients who underwent polysomnography had obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) (2 severe, 4 moderate, 5 mild). Findings suggestive of DW were observed in 25% of patients with IIM and exclusively in those with DM, while OSA was identified in all patients who underwent polysomnography. These findings may support the clinical evaluation of both diaphragm involvement and sleep-related breathing disorders in patients with IIM.

items.title: A Rare Case of Cystic Bronchiectasis With Concurrent Pulmonary Aspergillosis in a Rheumatoid Arthritis Patient Receiving Etanercept.
items.abstract: Tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) is critical to the body's ability to mount an appropriate inflammatory and immune response to various infections, particularly against intracellular organisms. As such, the immunosuppressive effects associated with TNF-α inhibitors, such as etanercept, may increase susceptibility to opportunistic infections. We report a case of pulmonary Aspergillus infection in a 47-year-old female with rheumatoid arthritis receiving etanercept who was found to have underlying cystic bronchiectatic changes. The patient presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and was subsequently found to have right lower lobe cystic bronchiectatic changes with mass-like densities on computed tomography (CT) imaging. Sputum fungal culture was positive for Aspergillus , bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) was positive for Aspergillus antigen, and fungal culture from a bronchoscopic biopsy specimen grew Aspergillus fumigatus . Other infectious evaluations were negative. The patient was treated with voriconazole, and etanercept was discontinued. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of interpreting Aspergillus isolation in patients with underlying structural lung disease and TNF-α inhibitor exposure.

items.title: The Many Faces of Familial Mediterranean Fever in Children: Lessons From a Moroccan Cohort and Four Diagnostic Pitfalls.
items.abstract: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is the prototypical hereditary autoinflammatory disease. Inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, it is associated with mutations in the MEditerranean FeVer (MEFV) gene. Its clinical heterogeneity poses a major diagnostic challenge in pediatrics, particularly in developing countries where access to genetic testing remains limited. To describe the clinical, epidemiological, biological, and genetic characteristics of pediatric FMF in the Oriental region of Morocco and to document diagnostic pitfalls through illustrative case reports. A retrospective descriptive study including 14 children followed for FMF in the Pediatrics Department of the Mohammed VI University Hospital in Oujda over an 11.5-year period (January 2015 to June 2026). The diagnosis was based on the Yalçınkaya-Özen pediatric criteria and/or genetic confirmation via MEFV gene sequencing. The mean age at diagnosis was 6.5 years (range: 2-14 years). A marked male predominance was observed in 12 (85.7%); sex ratio (6:1). Parental consanguinity was present in 5/14 (35.7%) of cases. All patients were from the Oriental region 14/14 (100.0%). The predominant clinical manifestations were recurrent fever in 14 (100.0%), abdominal pain in 12/14 (85.7%), and arthralgia/arthritis in 11/14 (78.6%). MEFV gene sequencing was positive in 9/14 (64.3%) of patients, with a predominance of the M694V mutation in 5/14 (35.7%), of whom 3/5 (60.0%) were homozygous. Four illustrative case reports document atypical presentations that resulted in a diagnostic delay of more than two years: a polyarticular form mimicking juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), a coronary aneurysm mistaken for Kawasaki disease, recurrent febrile seizures, and predominantly erysipelas-like erythema. Colchicine was effective in all 14/14 (100.0%) treated cases. No amyloid amyloidosis (AA) was detected during follow-up. Pediatric FMF is underdiagnosed in the Oriental region of Morocco. Its clinical polymorphism leads to diagnostic delays with harmful consequences. A rigorous clinical evaluation supported by targeted genetic sequencing is essential for early diagnosis and prompt initiation of colchicine therapy.

items.title: Pulmonary Manifestations in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis Presenting With Respiratory Symptoms at a Tertiary Care Center in Central India: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic inflammatory disease that, beyond its classical articular manifestations, frequently involves the lungs. Pulmonary complications, including interstitial lung disease (ILD), pleural disease, airway disease, and pulmonary vascular involvement, are important extra-articular manifestations that contribute substantially to disease morbidity. Many affected patients, however, remain clinically asymptomatic despite radiological or functional abnormalities. The primary objective was to characterize the clinical, functional, and radiological pulmonary findings among patients with RA presenting with respiratory symptoms. The secondary objective was to assess the association of pulmonary function test (PFT) and high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) abnormalities with disease duration and six-minute walk test (6MWT) distance. This cross-sectional observational study was conducted in the Department of General Medicine at a tertiary care, research, and teaching institute over two years (August 2024 to August 2026). Sixty-five consecutive patients aged >18 years with RA diagnosed according to the 2010 American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (ACR/EULAR) classification criteria and presenting with respiratory symptoms were enrolled by convenience sampling after excluding patients with pre-existing pulmonary disease or a connective tissue disorder other than RA. All patients underwent hematological and serological investigations, a 6MWT, spirometry, chest radiography, and HRCT of the chest. Disease activity was assessed using the Disease Activity Score-28 (DAS-28). Unadjusted associations were assessed using the chi-square test, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Females constituted 72.3% (47/65) of the cohort, and the 41-60-year age group accounted for more than half of the participants (35/65, 53.8%). The mean duration of RA at presentation was 7.1 ± 3.79 years. Chronic cough (43/65, 66.2%) and exertional dyspnea (30/65, 46.1%) were the most common respiratory symptoms, although 46% of patients (30/65) had no abnormal findings on chest auscultation. A restrictive pattern was the most common PFT abnormality (33/65, 50.8%), while a usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern was the most common abnormal HRCT finding (14/65, 21.5%). Longer disease duration was significantly associated with abnormal PFT findings (χ² = 7.98, df = 3, p = 0.047) and abnormal HRCT findings (χ² = 9.89, df = 3, p = 0.02). Shorter 6MWT distance was significantly associated with abnormal PFT findings (χ² = 20.43, df = 2, p < 0.001) and abnormal HRCT findings (χ² = 10.95, df = 2, p = 0.004). In this single-center sample of patients with RA presenting with respiratory symptoms, PFT and HRCT abnormalities were common, and longer disease duration and shorter 6MWT distance were associated with abnormal PFT and HRCT findings. These unadjusted cross-sectional associations do not establish causation or predictive value, and the findings cannot be used to estimate the prevalence of pulmonary involvement among all patients with RA. Prospective studies with adjustment for potential confounders are needed.

items.title: A Prospective Observational Study: Does Ramadan Fasting Worsen Rheumatoid Arthritis Disease Activity?
items.abstract: The impact of Ramadan fasting on rheumatoid arthritis (RA) disease activity remains insufficiently documented, and available data are limited. This study aimed to assess the effect of Ramadan fasting on RA disease activity in patients deemed fit to fast. Secondary objectives were to explore factors potentially associated with worsening disease activity during Ramadan and to assess treatment adherence before and after Ramadan. We conducted a prospective, observational, single-center study in the Rheumatology B Department of El Ayachi Hospital, Ibn Sina University Hospital Center, Rabat, Morocco, during Ramadan 2026. Patients over 18 years of age with RA meeting the American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (ACR/EULAR) classification criteria and deemed fit to fast were recruited consecutively during the month preceding Ramadan. Disease activity was assessed before and after Ramadan using clinical and biological parameters, including tender and swollen joint counts, morning stiffness, nocturnal awakenings, pain visual analog scale (VAS), fatigue, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and DAS28-ESR. The primary endpoint was the change in 28-joint Disease Activity Score (DAS28) between the pre- and post-Ramadan assessments. An exploratory univariate analysis was performed to identify factors associated with worsening disease activity. Treatment adherence was assessed before and after Ramadan using the four-item Morisky-Green-Levine scale. A total of 50 patients were included in the study. The mean age was 55.96 ± 10.40 years, and 44 patients (88.0%) were women. No statistically significant change in overall disease activity was observed before and after Ramadan. DAS28 changed from 2.85 ± 1.28 to 2.96 ± 1.31 (p = 0.481). No significant differences were found in pain VAS, nocturnal awakenings, fatigue, morning stiffness, tender joint count, swollen joint count, ESR, or CRP. Overall, 38 patients (76.0%) showed no worsening of disease activity, while 12 patients (24.0%) showed worsening. Worsening was associated with longer RA duration (18.13 ± 6.49 vs. 12.54 ± 9.77 years; p = 0.023) and lower baseline DAS28 (2.33 ± 0.81 vs. 3.01 ± 1.16; p = 0.031). High treatment adherence was observed in 47 patients (94.0%) before Ramadan and 46 patients (92.0%) after Ramadan. Ramadan fasting was not associated with a statistically significant worsening of RA disease activity. Most patients remained clinically stable, and treatment adherence remained high before and after Ramadan. These findings suggest that Ramadan fasting may be well tolerated in patients with RA who are deemed fit to fast and receive appropriate clinical follow-up.

items.title: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis Cases Associated with Leukotriene Receptor Antagonist Use with a Focus on Drug Type, Temporal Drug-Disease Relationship, Steroid-Tapering Status, and Antineutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody Positivity: A Systematic Literature Review.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) cases associated with leukotriene receptor antagonist (LTRA) use in asthmatic patients are well recognized. We reviewed LTRA-associated EGPA cases, focusing on LTRA types, drug-disease association patterns, steroidtapering status, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA) status. A systematic literature search was conducted to identify LTRA-associated EGPA cases. Cases were classified according to LTRA type, categorization according to the LTRA-EGPA temporal relationship (as outlined in Masi-Hamilos's article), systemic and/or steroid-tapering status for asthma, and ANCA positivity. Logistic regression analyses were used to determine whether specific clinical features were more common in specific subgroups. Ninety-five patients were identified. Montelukast was used in 65 cases, zafirlukast in 19, and pranlukast in 11. Masi-Hamilos categories: 60 patients in category A, 19 patients in category B, 11 patients in category C, and 5 patients in category D. Twenty-four patients received no steroids prior to EGPA diagnosis, 47 patients received a stable dose of oral and/ or inhaled steroids, and 24 patients had undergone tapering of oral and/ or inhaled steroids before EGPA onset. Of 80 patients with ANCA testing, 32 were ANCA positive. Logistic regression analyses demonstrated higher probabilities of pulmonary infiltrates and cardiomyopathy in EGPA cases associated with zafirlukast use, and an increased probability of sinusitis in Masi-Hamilos C and D categories. While certain clinical features of LTRA-associated EGPA varied across LTRA types and Masi-Hamilos categories, the rarity of cases and the low quality of evidence preclude us from reaching widespread conclusions.

items.title: Autoantibody Repertoire in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Advances, Challenges, and Clinical Perspectives.
items.abstract: This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the autoantibody repertoire in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and its clinical relevance. Autoantibody testing remains central to diagnosis and disease classification, with rheumatoid factor (RF) and antibodies to citrullinated proteins representing the most widely used serological markers. However, these conventional biomarkers do not fully capture the heterogeneity of the disease, and a substantial proportion of patients remain seronegative. In recent years, several emerging autoantibodies, including anti-carbamylated protein antibodies, anti-peptidylarginine deiminase 4 antibodies, anti-RA33, and anti-14-3-3η, have shown potential value as complementary biomarkers, particularly in early or seronegative disease. Some autoantibodies may also be detectable before the onset of clinically apparent arthritis, supporting a possible role in risk assessment and disease stratification. At the same time, their broader clinical application remains limited by assay heterogeneity, non-uniform diagnostic thresholds, and insufficient prospective validation. Overall, established and emerging autoantibodies provide important insight into diagnosis and disease subsets in RA, but further standardization is needed before wider clinical implementation.

items.title: Causal Associations Between Autoimmune Diseases and Renal Failure: A Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization Study with Mediation Analysis of Rheumatoid Arthritis and Glomerulonephritis.
items.abstract: Autoimmune diseases are frequently associated with renal involvement; however, their causal relationships with renal failure remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the causal effects of multiple autoimmune diseases on renal failure and explore the mediating role of glomerulonephritis using Mendelian randomization (MR). Summary statistics for systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjögren syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, and systemic sclerosis were retrieved from the IEU Open genome wide association studies project. Renal failure was defined as the study outcome. A two-sample MR framework was applied using the inverse variance weighted (IVW), weighted median, and MR-Egger methods, with additional sensitivity analyses performed to assess heterogeneity and horizontal pleiotropy. Furthermore, a mediation MR model was implemented in which rheumatoid arthritis was treated as the exposure, glomerulonephritis as the mediator, and renal failure as the outcome. No significant causal associations with renal failure were observed for systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjögren syndrome, or systemic sclerosis. In contrast, genetically predicted rheumatoid arthritis was associated with an increased risk of renal failure (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.05-1.18, P = 0.0005). Mediation analysis revealed a significant indirect effect of glomerulonephritis on the pathway from rheumatoid arthritis to renal failure (P = 3.07 × 10-7). This study provides genetic evidence supporting a causal link between rheumatoid arthritis and renal failure, with glomerulonephritis serving as an important potential genetic mediator of this association. These findings underscore the importance of early renal monitoring and management in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.

items.title: Effectiveness, safety and persistence of filgotinib in rheumatoid arthritis with a specific focus on difficult-to-treat patients: results from a multicentre observational study.
items.abstract: Filgotinib, a preferential JAK1 inhibitor, is among the most recently approved therapies for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Real-world evidence remains limited, particularly for difficult-to-treat RA (D2T) patients, who are underrepresented in clinical trials. We therefore evaluated the efficacy, safety, and treatment persistence of filgotinib in a large cohort of patients with RA, with a specific focus on those with D2T RA. This retrospective multicentre study included patients with RA (ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria) treated with filgotinib across nine Italian centres. Patients were followed every 3-6 months for up to 3 years, with collection of clinical variables, laboratory data, and adverse events (AEs). A total of 254 patients were included (mean age 58 ± 12 years; 85% female), of whom 47% had D2T disease. Disease activity indices (CDAI, DAS28-CRP, PGA, PhGA) improved significantly from baseline (p < 0.001), with remission rates reaching 41.3% (CDAI) and 70.5% (DAS28-CRP). Glucocorticoid (GC) use decreased from 64.4% to 32.6%. Improvements in disease activity and the GC-sparing effect were comparable between D2T RA and non-D2T RA patients. During follow-up, 153 AEs were reported, including 13 serious AEs and one infection-related death; non-serious infections were the most frequent events. Lipid profile remained stable throughout the study period, and two major cardiovascular events were reported. Treatment persistence was 88.4% at 6 months and 68% at 24 months, with no significant differences between D2T RA and non-D2T RA patients. Filgotinib demonstrated effective disease control, good safety and high treatment persistence in a real-world RA population, including a high proportion of D2T patients.

items.title: IgG4-related lung disease and seropositive undifferentiated arthritis in a patient initially presenting with monoarthritis: a case report.
items.abstract: IgG4-related lung disease (IgG4-RLD) is a fibroinflammatory pulmonary manifestation of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD). Its comorbidity with seropositive undifferentiated arthritis (SUA) is rare and may be overlooked due to overlapping clinical and immunological features. A 71-year-old man with acute left knee pain secondary to a meniscal tear with synovitis, as confirmed by MRI, was scheduled for arthroscopy. A preoperative chest radiograph incidentally revealed diffuse right lung lesions. Laboratory studies showed elevated rheumatoid factor (RF) and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies. The first multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion established a diagnosis of SUA and initiated disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) therapy, which resolved the arthralgia but did not improve the lung lesions. A subsequent MDT review, incorporating chest CT findings (thickened bronchovascular bundles and consolidation) and lung biopsy results, confirmed the diagnosis of IgG4-RLD. Treatment was then adjusted to high-dose glucocorticoids combined with DMARDs. Both pulmonary and articular manifestations showed significant remission. This rare case of IgG4-RLD complicating SUA highlights the importance of considering IgG4-RLD in patients with seropositive inflammatory arthritis presenting with atypical pulmonary imaging findings, particularly when lung lesions fail to respond to conventional DMARD therapy. MDT collaboration is essential for accurate diagnosis and optimal management of these concomitant autoimmune conditions.

items.title: Gaps in care for hydroxychloroquine retinopathy screening in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus or rheumatoid arthritis: a population-based cohort study.
items.abstract: Guideline-concordant screenings for hydroxychloroquine retinopathy (HCQ-R) are essential for safe long-term use of HCQ. We assessed adherence to the HCQ-R screening recommendations among patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and evaluated patient- and health system-level predictors of adherence. We conducted a longitudinal population-based cohort study (1997-2023) using linked British Columbia administrative health data capturing all physician and hospital encounters, tests billed, pharmacy-dispensed medications, and demographics. Using previously published algorithms, we identified all adults with SLE or RA who initiated HCQ after diagnosis and remained on therapy continuously for ≥ 1 year. Guideline-concordant (valid) screening was defined as a retinal visit (ICD-9 362.xx) with spectral domain optical coherence tomography and/or visual field-testing fee(s) (22067/02043) within a ± 30-day window, from baseline (HCQ initiation) until 31-Dec-2023, HCQ cessation, or censoring. Population-level adherence was assessed based on baseline and annual rates of valid screening. Patient-level adherence was assessed as the mean cumulative count of valid screenings received by each year of follow-up, with 95% CIs. Predictors of annual valid screening, including physician-care patterns (continuous vs. noncontinuous rheumatology vs. family-physician care), health authority regions, socioeconomic status (SES) and baseline screening, were assessed via multivariable generalized estimating equations adjusted for demographics and comorbidities. Of the 28,301 eligible patients for screening, 24% completed a valid baseline screening within year 1; during years 2-25, the annual rate of valid screenings ranged from 20 to 35%, and 70% remained unscreened on average. By 15 years, patients received on average 2.7 (95% CI, 2.6-2.8) valid screenings compared with at least 12 expected by this time, as recommended by the guidelines. Having a baseline screening was the strongest predictor of subsequent annual screenings (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 5.71; 95% CI: 4.89-6.67). Compared with continuous rheumatology care, family physician care had lower odds of screening (aOR, 0.59; 0.49-0.72). Most regions had lower screening rates than did Vancouver Coastal Health (9.50%-24.57%), with the lowest screening rate in Island Health (aOR, 0.39; 0.30-0.51). SES was not significantly associated with the odds of receiving annual screening. Guideline-recommended HCQ-R screening adherence was consistently low within a publicly funded health-care system; on average, one-fourth of patients on long-term HCQ, completed a valid screening annually. Strategies to strengthen guideline-based practices and reduce regional disparities are needed.

items.title: Evolving role of Anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies in rheumatoid arthritis: efficacy, safety, economic perspectives, and future directions-a narrative review.
items.abstract: B-cell depletion has established an important therapeutic role in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), particularly in selected patients with an inadequate response to tumor necrosis factor inhibitors or with clinical features favoring rituximab. However, the optimal positioning of anti-CD20 therapy remains constrained by heterogeneous treatment responses, cumulative immunosuppression, retreatment strategies, and differences in treatment accessibility. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from randomized controlled trials, long-term extension studies, real-world cohorts, mechanistic investigations, biosimilar studies, and pharmacoeconomic evaluations. Rituximab remains the only anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody with an established clinical role in RA. Newer-generation agents, including ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, and obinutuzumab, incorporate humanized, fully human, or glycoengineered designs that modify antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, complement-dependent cytotoxicity, direct cell death, and immunogenicity. Nevertheless, greater B-cell-depleting potency has not consistently translated into an acceptable long-term benefit-risk profile in RA. This discrepancy is described here as a "next-generation paradox," reflecting the narrower safety margin required in chronic autoimmune disease than in hematological malignancies. Rituximab biosimilars may improve treatment accessibility, although their economic impact is strongly dependent on regional procurement and reimbursement systems. Biomarker-guided patient selection, ultra-low-dose maintenance regimens, and dual targeting of B cells and BAFF axis represent promising approaches to treatment optimization., but their routine use remains limited by heterogeneous and, in some cases, non-RA-specific evidence. Rituximab retains clinically relevant value in carefully selected patients with RA, particularly seropositive patients and those for whom alternative targeted therapies are unsuitable. Future research should prioritize RA-specific prospective validation of biomarkers, individualized retreatment strategies, long-term immune safety, and regionally relevant pharmacoeconomic models rather than simply pursuing more potent B-cell depletion.

items.title: Novel Autoantibodies in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Translational Prospects from Seronegative Breakthrough to Precision Diagnosis and Treatment.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease characterized by chronic, erosive synovitis. While significant progress and breakthroughs have been made in disease diagnosis through basic research and clinical practice, approximately 30%-40% of seronegative RA patients still experience diagnostic delays and fail to achieve treatment targets. In recent years, the discovery of novel autoantibodies and biomarkers has opened new avenues for addressing this challenge. These molecules target post-translationally modified (PTM) antigens other than citrullinated proteins, while some are recognized independently of PTMs. They are also linked to key pathological processes such as inflammation, metabolism, and signal transduction. Experimental and clinical evidence directly or indirectly supports their regulatory roles in these processes. This review systematically summarizes the discovery process, target antigen functions, diagnostic efficacy, and roles in the pathogenesis of these novel antibodies. It focuses on their significant potential to improve the diagnosis rate of seronegative RA, predict disease progression and bone erosion risk, as well as define new disease subtypes. However, the precise mechanisms by which these autoantibodies contribute to RA pathogenesis remain to be fully elucidated. Furthermore, this article discusses current challenges, including detection standardization and clinical validation, and offers an outlook on the prospects for precision diagnosis and personalized treatment based on multi-autoantibody panels.

items.title: Application and cross-cultural validation of the ASAS HI-based health state utility algorithm in Chinese patients with spondyloarthritis.
items.abstract: Health State Utility (HSU) reflects individual preferences for specific health states and serve as a core parameter in health economic evaluations. Spondyloarthritis (SpA), a group of rheumatic diseases characterized by chronic back pain and joint involvement, imposes a substantial disease burden due to its progressive functional impairment and high healthcare costs. Accurate assessment of HSU in SpA patients is essential for a comprehensive understanding of disease burden, the development of targeted treatment strategies, and the optimization of healthcare resource allocation. A SpA-specific HSU algorithm based on the Assessment of Spondyloarthritis international Society Health Index (ASAS HI) has been developed and preliminarily validated in several European countries, yet no empirical studies have examined its applicability in China. Therefore, the aim of this study was to determine the applicability of this HSU algorithm to Chinese patients with SpA, and to assess its consistency with the Time Trade-Off (TTO) method and the Five-Level EuroQoL five dimensions (EQ-5D-5 L), providing methodological support for health economic evaluations in this population. The study involved 102 SpA patients. Health state utility values (HSUVs) were assessed using the TTO, EQ-5D-5 L, and ASAS HI algorithms, respectively. Descriptive statistics were performed, followed by evaluations of convergent and discriminant validity for the ASAS HI algorithm. Consistency among these methods was tested using Bland-Altman analysis, ICC, and linear regression models. Finally, a sensitivity analysis was conducted through age stratification to further verify the robustness of the results. HSUVs calculated by different algorithms ranged from 0.67 to 0.78. The HSUV derived from ASAS HI was significantly positive correlated with TTO and EQ-5D-5 L score, which has low correlation with unrelated variables. Bland-Altman analysis showed that most differences fell within ± 1.96 standard deviations. The ICC exceeded 0.7, and the coefficient of determination for the linear regression model was 0.63 and 0.80, respectively. Sensitivity analysis also indicated that the research results have good stability among different age groups. The ASAS HI-based HSUV algorithm demonstrates good validity and high consistency with TTO and EQ-5D-5 L in Chinese SpA patients. It can serve as a reliable tool for HSUV assessment in this population.

items.title: Defining the optimal interferon-stimulated genes panel to reflect serum interferon-α levels in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: The type I interferon-alpha (IFN-α) gene expression signature refers to the analysis of specific IFN-stimulated genes (ISG) as a surrogate measure of IFN-α pathway activity. It is widely used to assess IFN-α activity in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), as well as to evaluate treatment response or serve as an index of disease activity. ISGs are often aggregated into a composite score that provides a quantitative measure. However, previous literature has employed differing combinations of ISG, and no clear consensus exists regarding which should be preferentially used. Our study aims to identify the combination of IGS that best correlates with serum IFN-α levels in patients with SLE. A total of 252 patients with SLE were recruited in this cross-sectional study. IFN-α serum levels were measured using Simoa (Single Molecule Array) technique. Based on prior literature, 72 transcripts previously used in other studies in rheumatic musculoskeletal diseases were selected and analyzed by qPCR using Nanostring ® technology. Fifty-one distinct IFN scores were computed using previously reported ISG combinations. Besides, LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression analysis was performed to identify the minimal and most parsimonious combination of ISGs associated with serum IFN-α levels. LASSO analysis identified a 13-ISG combination as the most parsimonious predictor of serum IFN-α levels. However, the IFN score constructed using these 13 genes showed lower correlation with serum IFN-α levels than previously reported IFN scores from the literature. This suggests that statistically derived ISG selection is inferior to mechanistically- or pathophysiologically-informed gene combinations. Three literature-derived ISG combinations-IFI44L IFIT1 RSAD2 IFI27 ISG15 SIGLEC1, IFI27 IFI44 IFI44L RSAD2, and IFI44L IFI44 RSAD2 IFI27 IFI6-demonstrated high IFN-α correlations, statistically indistinguishable from each other but significantly superior to the remaining 48 combinations. This study provides evidence-based recommendations for ISG selection in constructing optimal IFN signatures to accurately predict serum IFN-α levels in SLE patients.

items.title: Turner syndrome complicating osteogenesis imperfecta, thyroiditis and ankylosing spondylitis: a case report.
items.abstract: Turner syndrome (TS) is a chromosomal disorder characterized by monosomy of the X chromosome (45,X0) or structural aberrations in one of the X chromosomes in individuals with a female phenotype. Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI), commonly known as brittle bone disease, results from genetic abnormalities that lead to altered metabolism, reduced quantity, or structural defects in type I collagen, ultimately causing abnormal bone architecture, recurrent fractures, and progressive skeletal deformities. We report a 27-year-old Chinese woman with TS (45,X0) and a history of osteoporosis and uveitis who presented with 11 years of low back pain and one month of bilateral ankle swelling. She had previously undergone spinal fixation and bilateral hip replacement. Examination revealed blue sclerae, height 132 cm, and weight 26 kg. Laboratory findings showed elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR, 52 mm/hour) and C-reactive protein (CRP, 75.9 mg/L), positive HLA-B27, and elevated thyroid antibodies. Imaging revealed sacroiliitis on computed tomography and enthesitis on ankle magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Genetic testing identified a heterozygous collagen type I α 1 chain (COL1A1) mutation and an Xp22.33-q28 deletion. She met the modified New York criteria for ankylosing spondylitis (AS). Treatment with adalimumab led to clinical improvement with decreased erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) after one month. This case highlights the rare co-occurrence of TS, OI, and AS, emphasizing the importance of genetic and rheumatologic evaluation in complex presentations. We recommend annual clinical assessment for inflammatory back pain and, when clinically indicated, sacroiliac imaging (such as MRI or X-ray) to facilitate early diagnosis and management of concurrent rheumatologic conditions.

items.title: Knockdown of the long isoform of the prolactin receptor selectively targets pathogenic immune cells in systemic lupus erythematosus and averts glomerular pathology.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by chronic inflammation in multiple organ systems. Although elevated circulating levels of the hormone/cytokine prolactin (PRL) have long been associated with increased SLE activity, the extent to which different isoforms of the prolactin receptor (PRLR) contribute to disease pathogenesis has not been explored. Here, we show that immune cells in SLE have aberrant splicing of the PRLR such that the ratio of the long (LF) to short (SF) splice isoforms is increased. To determine whether change in PRLR isoform expression was causal in this disease, we used a splice-modulating oligomer that knocks down expression of the LFPRLR while increasing expression of the SFPRLRs. Using patient samples ex vivo, SLE-prone mice in vivo, high-dimensional flow cytometry, and single-cell RNA sequencing, we demonstrated that the aberrant PRLR isoform expression in SLE both directly and indirectly contributes to the generation of autoreactive immune cell phenotypes. Accordingly, LFPRLR knockdown (KD) reduced STAT1 phosphorylation, decreased expression of type I interferon signaling/response genes known to be biomarkers and hub genes for SLE, reduced immunoglobulins with autoreactivity-associated sequence features, and averted glomerular pathology in SLE-prone mice. Importantly, LFPRLR KD reduced pathogenic B cell and other immune subsets that drive B cell activation, without negative impact on healthy donor counterparts. Current treatments for SLE adversely affect healthy cells and do not concurrently eradicate multiple pathogenic immune subsets. As LFPRLR splice-modulating oligomer does not share these disadvantages, KD of the LFPRLR represents a potential treatment strategy for SLE that merits further investigation. The long prolactin receptor (LFPRLR) represents an attractive therapeutic target in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Upper left: individuals with SLE exhibit aberrant increases in their relative transcript expression of the counteractive long (LF) to short (SF) PRLR isoforms. The aberrant increase in the ratio of LF:SF in SLE contributes to increased phosphorylation of STATs, predominantly STAT1. Upper right: aberrant increase in relative expression of LF:SF contributes to autoreactive immunophenotypes and glomerular pathology. Bottom: an SMO, which specifically prevents synthesis of only the LFPRLR and can increase expression of the counteractive SFs, tilts the balance of PRLR splice isoforms in favor of the SFs and reduces pathogenic signaling, immunophenotypes, and glomerular damage in SLE. Exons and introns are not drawn to scale. GC, germinal center; IFN-I, type I interferons; NK, natural killer; TLR, Toll-like receptor.

items.title: Diagnostic odyssey of juvenile onset primary Sjögren's disease: Recurrent neck swelling and rampant dental caries in a 17-year old female.
items.abstract: Primary Sjögren's disease is an exceedingly rare auto-immune disorder in paediatric and adolescent populations, frequently leading to prolonged diagnostic delays due to atypical initial presentations. We report a 17-year old female presenting with a four-year history of recurrent neck swelling, dysphagia, rampant dental caries and progressive xerostomia, previously misdiagnosed and managed empirically as viral infections and reactive lymphadenitis. Physical examination confirmed severe oral dryness and hyposalivation. Serological testing revealed positive antinuclear antibodies with high titers of anti-Ro (SSA) and anti-La (SSB). A labial minor salivary gland excision biopsy demonstrated focal lymphocytic sialadenitis, definitively confirming juvenile-onset primary Sjögren's disease.

items.title: Salivary Metabolomic Alterations in Primary Sjögren Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: This systematic review assesses the diagnostic potential of salivary metabolomics in discriminating between primary Sjögren disease (pSjD) and healthy controls, aiming to identify potential biomarkers for clinical application. A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus following the Centre for Reviews and Dissemination and PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Methodological quality was primarily assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy in OMICS (QUADOMICS) tool. Meta-analysis utilised random-effects models, with effect sizes presented via forest plots. Nine studies met criteria, displaying heterogeneous metabolite profiles. Meta-analysis of two studies with complete quantitative data revealed no significant differences in glycine, pyruvic acid or succinic acid levels between pSjD and controls. Glycine demonstrated substantial heterogeneity (I 2  = 81.2%), whereas pyruvic and succinic acids showed consistent pooled effects with no heterogeneity (I 2  = 0%). Evidence for succinic acid, pyruvic acid and glycine as salivary biomarkers remains insufficient. Although pSjD is associated with alterations in the salivary metabolome, the evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Further high-quality studies are required to clarify their diagnostic potential. pSjD saliva exhibits a metabolic 'shift', suggesting that salivary metabolomics may reflect disease-related alterations despite variability in individual metabolites.

items.title: Prevalence of Rheumatoid Arthritis, Osteoarthritis and Gout among Alaska Native/American Indian Peoples in Alaska.
items.abstract: The objective of this study was to determine the prevalence of three common forms of arthritis (rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, and gout) in Alaska Native and American Indian (AN/AI) peoples of Alaska. We identified adults with a potential diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, or gout based on queries of the electronic health records within participating organizations in the Alaska Tribal Health System based on ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes. We performed medical record abstraction for a subset of individuals with potential arthritis to confirm the diagnosis, classification criteria documented in the medical record, and associated clinical features. We applied the validation results to the full sample of adults with potential arthritis identified from electronic health record queries to estimate the point prevalence of each form of arthritis as of December 31, 2019. Of the three types of arthritis, osteoarthritis was the most common (overall age-adjusted prevalence 14.0% (95% CI 13.2-14.8%)), followed by rheumatoid arthritis (overall age-adjusted prevalence 2.39% (95% CI 2.19-2.60%)), then gout (overall age-adjusted prevalence 1.33% (95% CI 1.20-1.47%)). Osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis were more common in women than men, while gout was more common in men than women. The prevalence of all three types of arthritis increased with age. Compared to U.S. or global population-based studies, the prevalence of osteoarthritis in AN/AI peoples of Alaska is similar, while the prevalence of gout is lower than expected and the prevalence of rheumatoid arthritis is high and similar to prior studies in this population.

items.title: Childhood Adversity and Self-Reported Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Structural Equation Modeling Analysis of the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging.
items.abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the association between adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and self-reported rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and to investigate potential psychosocial and behavioural mediators of this relationship. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses (EFA; CFA) were conducted to assess the dimensionality of ACEs. Hypothesized direct and indirect pathways from a latent ACEs construct to RA were tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) with data (N = 44,142) from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging. Putative mediation through depression, anxiety, obesity, and smoking was examined. Analyses adjusted for sociodemographic factors, asthma, and childhood passive smoking. Moderation by birth sex was tested with multigroup SEM. EFA and CFA supported a higher-order latent childhood adversity factor with three first-order factors (physical abuse, sexual abuse, household dysfunction). SEM showed a small but significant direct ACEs-RA association, as well as significant associations operating through depression, obesity, and smoking. Birth sex appeared to moderate the indirect pathway through obesity, with a stronger association for men. An indirect association through smoking was observed only in men, though the between-group difference was not statistically significant. ACEs were significantly associated with self-reported RA, partially through indirect pathways involving depression, obesity, and smoking, with evidence of sex-specific effects on the obesity pathway. Targeted screening and intervention for ACEs-affected individuals with psychosocial and behavioural risk factors may help reduce RA burden. Prospective mediation research examining gene-environment interactions (e.g., smoking × RA risk alleles) and sex-specific mechanisms is warranted.

items.title: Predictors of Clinical Remission in Children With Polyarticular Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis Treated With Abatacept.
items.abstract: To determine whether demographics, clinical measures, and disease activity predict inactive disease (ID) or clinical remission (CR) in patients with polyarticular course-juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pc-JIA) treated with abatacept. Data were extracted from 2 phase III clinical trials in pc-JIA treated with intravenous (age 6-17 years; NCT00095173) and subcutaneous (age 2-17 years; NCT01844518) abatacept. Efficacy endpoints were Juvenile Arthritis Disease Activity Score 10 (JADAS) ID (score ≤2.7) and JADAS CR, (6 consecutive months of JADAS ID based on C-reactive protein [CRP] levels). Time-to-event analyses were performed. Kaplan-Meier analyses estimated time to achieve CR and ID. A total of 347/409 (84.8%) patients were included: 128/190 (67.4%) from the intravenous abatacept trial (excluded: 62 patients who switched to placebo) and 219/219 (100%) from the subcutaneous abatacept trial. In the multivariable model, baseline predictors of JADAS CR (hazard ratio [HR]) included younger age (≤10 years; 1.8), lower CHAQ-DI (≤0.75; 1.8), lower parent global assessment values (≤43.16; 2.1), and normal high-sensitivity CRP (<0.21; 1.6). Patients with minimal disease activity at days 57 or 85 were more likely to achieve both JADAS ID (HR [reference: minimal disease activity] 0.2-0.4 or 0.2-0.5, respectively) and CR (HR [reference: minimal disease activity] 0.1-0.5 or 0-0.3, respectively) earlier than patients with moderate or high disease activity during a 24-month period. Patients who achieve minimal disease activity within 3 months of abatacept treatment are more likely to achieve JADAS ID or CR earlier and maintain it for 24 months, regardless of administration route.

items.title: Discontinuation of systemic medications in Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis - Risks and Remission: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Safe and effective strategies for discontinuing systemic medications in children and adolescents with juvenile idiopathic arthritis remain to be defined. This study aimed to determine flare risks following medication discontinuation and to evaluate the impact of disease subtype, remission duration, medication class and discontinuation strategy. A systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO-CRD420251168572) was conducted using MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Web of Science evidence synthesis through October 2025. Included studies evaluated medication withdrawal-stopping versus tapering strategies in JIA patients (≤18 years) in remission. Flare was the primary outcome. Random-effects metaanalysis, subgroup analyses, meta-regression, and RoB 2 and ROBINS-I assessments were performed. 18 studies assessing 1,905 patients were included. Flare proportions ranged between 13%-78%, with a pooled estimate of 45% (95%CI:33%-56%;I²=97%). Lower proportions were observed with tapering, including interval spacing (25%[95%CI:8%-42%]) and dose reduction (42%[95%CI:18%-65%]) compared to stopping (57%[95%CI:44%-70%]); differences were not statistically significant. Tapering strategy was the only significant moderator of flare risk (β=0.26, p=0.02), explaining 19% of heterogeneity. Most flares occurred within 6-12 months. Flare proportions also varied by disease subtype, medication class, and remission duration before. Recapture of remission was reported in 50%-100% of patients. Incidence rate sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings (0.35 flares/person-year). Medication discontinuation in JIA carried significant flare risk across both cumulative proportion and person-year rates. The observed heterogeneity primarily mirrored the clinical variation in withdrawal strategies. Differences in flare proportions may reflect residual drug exposure rather than the true strategy effects. The high recapture rate provides reassurance for advancing medication discontinuation approaches.

items.title: Bimekizumab-Treated Patients with Axial Spondyloarthritis Maintained Stringent Clinical Responses Over 3 Years: Phase 3 and Open-Label Extension Results.
items.abstract: To assess the effect of bimekizumab, a dual inhibitor of IL-17F and IL-17A, on maintenance of stringent clinical response outcomes to three years in patients with axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) from two phase 3 studies and their open-label extension (OLE). Achievement of stringent clinical outcomes (Assessment of SpondyloArthritis international Society ≥40% improvement/partial remission [ASAS40/PR]), disease activity outcomes (Axial Spondyloarthritis Disease Activity Score low disease activity/inactive disease [ASDAS LDA/ID], Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index [BASDAI] <2), no/minimal or mild pain/fatigue (BASDAI Q1/Q2 <2/<4, respectively) and resolution of enthesitis (Maastricht Ankylosing Spondylitis Enthesitis Score [MASES]=0) are reported pooled across BE MOBILE 1 (non-radiographic [nr]-axSpA) and 2 (radiographic [r]-axSpA), to Week 164 for bimekizumab-randomised patients who achieved each outcome at Week 16. Data are descriptive, reported as non-responder imputation (NRI), modified NRI (mNRI), multiple imputation (MI) or observed case (OC). Of 349 bimekizumab-randomised patients, at Week 16, 45.8% achieved ASAS40, 24.6% ASAS PR, 43.6% ASDAS LDA, 16.6% ASDAS ID (NRI). The majority sustained achievement of these outcomes at Week 164 (80.4%/66.3%/78.8%/61.0%, respectively; mNRI/MI). Similar trends were observed for pain/fatigue reduction and resolution of enthesitis. Respectively, 36.2% and 38.0% who achieved ASDAS LDA and BASDAI <2 at Week 16 maintained their response at every visit to Week 164 (as observed). In this exploratory analysis, across the full axSpA disease spectrum, the majority of patients who achieved stringent clinical outcomes with bimekizumab treatment at Week 16 maintained their response over three years, supporting deep and sustained efficacy with long-term bimekizumab treatment.
